96387d7670fa405951cab55121b2e3c62aa2cf0e feat(agent): allow vouched symlinked agent config directories
A dotfile-managed .claude (chezmoi, stow, yadm) is an ordinary setup among
exactly the people who run coding agents, and the only answer Entire had
was to stop managing it that way.

allow_symlinked_agent_dirs in .entire/settings.local.json names
worktree-relative agent config directories whose symlinks are followed,
anchoring the root on the resolved target. Three properties keep it a
hatch rather than a hole.

It is a list, not a boolean: a flag disables the class, where naming a
path says which arrangement is the user's.

It has two independent boundaries. The same untracked-and-verified gate as
the OPF command and external_agents decides whether the FILE may grant --
a repository that could both ship the link and vouch for it is the whole
attack. A name check then decides whether the PATH is one an agent config
lives under, so .entire and .git/hooks are unspellable even from a
verified local file.

And the vouchable set is pinned rather than derived from
AllHookConfigRelPaths, which was the first version and was wrong twice:
that registry is mutable at runtime, so deriving would let an external
plugin widen what a user can be persuaded to vouch for, and it is empty in
a binary that has not imported the agent packages, so the set collapsed
depending on the caller's import graph.
TestVouchableDirsMatchTheBuiltInAgents catches drift both ways.

Vouching for a directory does not vouch for links inside it: below the
anchor everything is a name in a root again. The skill scaffolds go
through the same anchor, or enable half-applies across two directories. A
vouched but unresolvable link is an error, not a quiet fall back to
refusing. status prints what is followed and what was rejected, and doctor
reports it as FOLLOWING SYMLINKS rather than as a fault.

.entire, the settings files and the git hooks directory are deliberately
excluded. The settings case is circular -- a symlinked settings.local.json
vouching for symlinked settings files authorizes itself -- and the hooks
case already has git's own core.hooksPath.

   464		if !newTip.Equal(scan.LocalTip) {
   465			if err := atomicSetV1Ref(ctx, repo, scan.LocalTip, newTip); err != nil {
   466				return res, err
   467			}
   468			res.NewLocalTip = newTip
   469		}
   470	
   471		if !scan.RemoteTip.IsZero() && scan.RemoteAhead {
   472			before := rw.commitsRewritten
   473			fixedRemote, err := rw.rewriteHistory(scan.RemoteTip)
   474			if err != nil {
   475				return res, fmt.Errorf("rewrite %s/%s: %w", scan.RemoteName, v1.Short(), err)
   476			}
   477			res.RemoteCommitsRewritten = rw.commitsRewritten - before
   478			newTip, err = reconcileRewrittenTips(ctx, repo, w, scan.RemoteName, v1, newTip, fixedRemote)
   479			if err != nil {
   480				return res, err
   481			}
   482			res.NewLocalTip = newTip
   483		}
   484		res.BlobsShrunk = rw.blobsShrunk
   485		res.StillOversized = rw.stillOversized
   486		logging.Info(logCtx, "shrank oversized checkpoint metadata",
   487			slog.String("old_tip", scan.LocalTip.String()),
   488			slog.String("new_tip", newTip.String()),
   489			slog.Int("commits_rewritten", res.CommitsRewritten),
   490			slog.Int("remote_commits_rewritten", res.RemoteCommitsRewritten),
   491			slog.Int("blobs_shrunk", rw.blobsShrunk))
   492	
   493		switch {
   494		case scan.RemoteName == "":
   495			res.PushSkippedReason = "no checkpoint sync remote is configured"
   496		case scan.RemoteTip.IsZero() && scan.RemoteErr != nil:
   497			res.PushSkippedReason = fmt.Sprintf("the state of %s could not be determined (%v); re-run entire doctor once it is reachable", scan.RemoteName, scan.RemoteErr)
   498		case scan.RemoteTip.IsZero():
   499			res.PushSkippedReason = fmt.Sprintf("%s has no %s branch yet; the next git push creates it", scan.RemoteName, v1.Short())
   500		case scan.RemoteTip.Equal(newTip):
   501			res.PushSkippedReason = scan.RemoteName + " already has this history"
   502		case scan.PushDisabled:
   503			res.PushSkippedReason = "checkpoint pushing is disabled in settings; push the branch yourself with --force-with-lease"
   504		default:
   505			if err := forcePushCheckpointBranch(ctx, scan.RemoteName, v1, scan.RemoteTip, newTip); err != nil {
   506				return res, &PushFailedError{Remote: scan.RemoteName, Err: err}
   507			}
   508			res.Pushed = true
   509		}
   510		return res, nil
   511	}
   512	
   513	// reconcileRewrittenTips brings the local branch (at rewritten tip local) and
   514	// the rewritten remote history (fixedRemote) together and returns the new
   515	// local tip. Three cases, decided on content rather than hashes because
   516	// independent rewrites of the same history differ in hash when commit signing
   517	// is on:
   518	//
   519	//   - the remote already holds everything local has (local's tree appears in
   520	//     the remote's history): adopt the remote tip, no replay;
   521	//   - local already holds everything the remote has: keep local, which the
   522	//     caller then pushes;
   523	//   - genuine divergence: replay the local-only commits onto the remote via
   524	//     SafelyAdvanceLocalRef, the same reconciliation pre-push uses.
   525	func reconcileRewrittenTips(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, w io.Writer, remoteName string, v1 plumbing.ReferenceName, local, fixedRemote plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   526		if fixedRemote.Equal(local) {
   527			return local, nil
   528		}
   529		if local.IsZero() {
   530			if err := SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, v1, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   531				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("adopt %s/%s: %w", remoteName, v1.Short(), err)
   532			}
   533			return fixedRemote, nil
   534		}
   535		remoteHasLocal, err := contentReachable(repo, fixedRemote, local)
   536		if err != nil {
   537			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   538		}
   539		if remoteHasLocal {
   540			fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Remote %s already holds every local checkpoint; adopting its history.\n", remoteName)
   541			if err := atomicSetV1Ref(ctx, repo, local, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   542				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   543			}
   544			return fixedRemote, nil
   545		}
   546		localHasRemote, err := contentReachable(repo, local, fixedRemote)
   547		if err != nil {
   548			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   549		}
   550		if localHasRemote {
   551			return local, nil
   552		}
   553		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Remote %s has checkpoints not yet local; replaying local checkpoints onto it.\n", remoteName)
   554		if err := SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, v1, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   555			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("reconcile local %s with %s: %w", v1.Short(), remoteName, err)
   556		}
   557		tip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   558		if err != nil {
   559			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("re-read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   560		}
   561		return tip, nil
   562	}
   563	
   564	// forcePushCheckpointBranch replaces the remote's checkpoint branch with newTip,
   565	// refusing (via --force-with-lease) if the remote no longer sits at expected.
   566	func forcePushCheckpointBranch(ctx context.Context, remoteName string, branch plumbing.ReferenceName, expected, newTip plumbing.Hash) error {
   567		pushCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
   568		defer cancel()
   569		_, err := remote.PushWithOptions(pushCtx, remote.PushOptions{
   570			Remote:    remoteName,
   571			RefSpecs:  []string{newTip.String() + ":" + branch.String()},
   572			ExtraArgs: []string{"--force-with-lease=" + branch.String() + ":" + expected.String()},
   573		})
   574		if err != nil {
   575			return fmt.Errorf("force-push %s to %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, err)
   576		}
   577		return nil
   578	}
   579	
   580	// metadataRewriter rewrites a commit graph replacing oversized metadata.json
   581	// blobs. Every level is memoized: a blob is stripped once however many trees
   582	// reference it, a tree is rebuilt once however many commits share it, and a
   583	// commit is rewritten once however many children it has.
   584	type metadataRewriter struct {
   585		ctx       context.Context //nolint:containedctx // scoped to one rewrite; threaded into commit signing
   586		repo      *git.Repository
   587		threshold int64
   588	
   589		blobs   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   590		trees   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   598	func newMetadataRewriter(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, threshold int64) *metadataRewriter {
   599		return &metadataRewriter{
   600			ctx:       ctx,
   601			repo:      repo,
   602			threshold: threshold,
   603			blobs:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   604			trees:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   605			commits:   make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   606		}
   607	}
   608	
   609	// rewriteHistory returns the rewritten equivalent of tip. Parents are processed
   610	// before children with an explicit stack, so a branch with thousands of
   611	// checkpoints does not recurse thousands deep.
   612	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteHistory(tip plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   613		if tip.IsZero() {
   614			return tip, nil
   615		}
   616		type frame struct {
   617			hash     plumbing.Hash
   618			expanded bool
   619		}
   620		stack := []frame{{hash: tip}}
   621		for len(stack) > 0 {
   622			if err := r.ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   623				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err //nolint:wrapcheck // context cancellation propagates as-is
   624			}
   625			top := len(stack) - 1
   626			f := stack[top]
   627			if _, done := r.commits[f.hash]; done {
   628				stack = stack[:top]
   629				continue
   630			}
   631			c, err := r.repo.CommitObject(f.hash)
   632			if err != nil {
   633				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load commit %s: %w", f.hash, err)
   634			}
   635			if !f.expanded {
   636				stack[top].expanded = true
   637				for _, p := range c.ParentHashes {
   638					if _, done := r.commits[p]; !done {
   639						stack = append(stack, frame{hash: p})
   640					}
   641				}
   642				continue
   643			}
   644			newHash, err := r.rewriteCommit(c)
   645			if err != nil {
   646				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   647			}
   648			r.commits[f.hash] = newHash
   649			stack = stack[:top]
   650		}
   651		return r.commits[tip], nil
   652	}
   653	
   654	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteCommit(c *object.Commit) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   655		newTree, err := r.rewriteTree(c.TreeHash, "")
   656		if err != nil {
   657			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   658		}
   659		parents := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(c.ParentHashes))
   660		changed := !newTree.Equal(c.TreeHash)
   661		for _, p := range c.ParentHashes {
   662			np, ok := r.commits[p]
   663			if !ok {
   664				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("parent %s of %s was not rewritten first", p, c.Hash)
   665			}
   666			if !np.Equal(p) {
   667				changed = true
   668			}
   669			parents = append(parents, np)
   670		}
   671		if !changed {
   672			return c.Hash, nil
   673		}
   674		rewritten := &object.Commit{
   675			Author:       c.Author,
   676			Committer:    c.Committer,
   677			Message:      c.Message,
   678			TreeHash:     newTree,
   679			ParentHashes: parents,
   680			Encoding:     c.Encoding,
   681			ExtraHeaders: c.ExtraHeaders,
   682		}
   683		// Re-sign when signing is configured: the original signature covered the
   684		// original tree, so it cannot be carried over. Signing makes the rewritten
   685		// hash non-deterministic across runs, which is why reconciliation below
   686		// compares trees (contentReachable) rather than hashes.
   687		checkpoint.SignCommitBestEffort(r.ctx, rewritten)
   688		obj := r.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   689		if err := rewritten.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   690			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode rewritten commit %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   691		}
   692		hash, err := r.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   693		if err != nil {
   694			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store rewritten commit %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   695		}
   696		r.commitsRewritten++
   697		return hash, nil
   698	}
   699	
   700	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteTree(hash plumbing.Hash, prefix string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   701		if done, ok := r.trees[hash]; ok {
   702			return done, nil
   703		}
   704		tree, err := r.repo.TreeObject(hash)
   705		if err != nil {
   706			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load tree %s: %w", hash, err)
   707		}
   708		entries := make([]object.TreeEntry, 0, len(tree.Entries))
   709		changed := false
   710		for _, e := range tree.Entries {
   711			entryPath := e.Name
   712			if prefix != "" {
   713				entryPath = prefix + "/" + e.Name
   714			}
   715			newEntry := e
   716			switch e.Mode {
   717			case filemode.Dir:
   718				sub, subErr := r.rewriteTree(e.Hash, entryPath)
   719				if subErr != nil {
   720					return plumbing.ZeroHash, subErr
   721				}
   722				newEntry.Hash = sub
   723			case filemode.Regular, filemode.Executable, filemode.Deprecated:
   724				if e.Name == paths.MetadataFileName {
   725					blob, blobErr := r.rewriteBlob(e.Hash, entryPath)
   726					if blobErr != nil {
   727						return plumbing.ZeroHash, blobErr
   728					}
   729					newEntry.Hash = blob
   730				}
   731			case filemode.Empty, filemode.Symlink, filemode.Submodule:
   732				// kept verbatim
   733			}
   734			if !newEntry.Hash.Equal(e.Hash) {
   735				changed = true
   736			}
   737			entries = append(entries, newEntry)
   738		}
   739		if !changed {
   740			r.trees[hash] = hash
   741			return hash, nil
   742		}
   743		newTree := &object.Tree{Entries: entries}
   744		obj := r.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   745		if err := newTree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   746			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode tree %s: %w", prefix, err)
   747		}
   748		newHash, err := r.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   749		if err != nil {
   750			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store tree %s: %w", prefix, err)
   751		}
   752		r.trees[hash] = newHash
   753		return newHash, nil
   754	}
   755	
   756	// rewriteBlob returns the replacement for a metadata.json blob: itself when it
   757	// is under the threshold or carries no prompt_attributions, else a copy without
   758	// that field.
   759	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteBlob(hash plumbing.Hash, blobPath string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   760		if done, ok := r.blobs[hash]; ok {
   761			return done, nil
   762		}
   763		blob, err := r.repo.BlobObject(hash)
   764		if err != nil {
   765			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, err)
   766		}
   767		if blob.Size <= r.threshold {
   768			r.blobs[hash] = hash
   769			return hash, nil
   770		}
   771		data, err := readBlob(r.repo, hash)
   772		if err != nil {
   773			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("read blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, err)
   774		}
   775		stripped, changed, err := stripPromptAttributions(data)
   776		if err != nil || !changed {
   777			// Either not the JSON this repair understands, or large for a reason
   778			// other than the field it knows how to remove: leave it and say so
   779			// rather than guess at what to delete.
   780			r.stillOversized = append(r.stillOversized, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: blob.Size, Hash: hash})
   781			r.blobs[hash] = hash
   782			return hash, nil //nolint:nilerr // deliberate: an unparseable blob is kept verbatim and reported via stillOversized
   783		}
   784		newHash, err := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(r.repo, stripped)
   785		if err != nil {
   786			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("write shrunk blob for %s: %w", blobPath, err)
   787		}
   788		r.blobsShrunk++
   789		if int64(len(stripped)) > r.threshold {
   790			r.stillOversized = append(r.stillOversized, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: int64(len(stripped)), Hash: newHash})
   791		}
   792		r.blobs[hash] = newHash
   793		return newHash, nil
   794	}
   795	
   796	// stripPromptAttributions removes the prompt_attributions key from a
   797	// metadata.json document, preserving every other field verbatim (as raw JSON),
   798	// and reports whether anything changed. Keys come back sorted, which is the one
   799	// cosmetic difference from the writer's field order.
   800	func stripPromptAttributions(data []byte) ([]byte, bool, error) {
   801		var doc map[string]json.RawMessage
   802		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &doc); err != nil {
   803			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("parse metadata.json: %w", err)
   804		}
   805		if _, ok := doc[promptAttributionsField]; !ok {
   806			return data, false, nil
   807		}
   808		delete(doc, promptAttributionsField)
   809		out, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(doc, "", "  ")
   810		if err != nil {
   811			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("re-encode metadata.json: %w", err)
   812		}
   813		return out, true, nil
   814	}

    27	// OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold is the blob size above which a
    28	// per-session metadata.json on entire/checkpoints/v1 is reported by
    29	// `entire doctor`. GitHub warns at 50 MiB and refuses any blob over 100 MiB, and
    30	// a refused blob anywhere in the branch's history makes the whole branch
    31	// unpushable there — including through a forge's push mirror. A healthy
    32	// metadata.json is tens of kilobytes, so anything past this line is the
    33	// pre-v0.10.1 prompt_attributions bloat (see checkpoint.MaxPromptAttributionsBytes),
    34	// not a large session.
    35	const OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold int64 = 50 << 20

    38	// the only field whose size scales with the working tree rather than the
    39	// session, and nothing reads it back — the attribution summary it fed is a
    40	// separate field that stays.

   110	// ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata refreshes the elected sync remote's tracking
   111	// ref for the checkpoint branch (best effort) and reports every metadata.json
   112	// blob over threshold reachable from the local branch or from that tracking ref.
   113	// It is read-only: nothing under refs/heads is touched.
   114	//
   115	// The remote side matters because the repair force-pushes: a blob that is only
   116	// on the remote (an earlier local repair whose push failed) still blocks the
   117	// mirror, and an ordinary pre-push would replay the local branch onto that
   118	// remote history and reintroduce it.
   119	//
   120	// The network is touched only when something is oversized. The local branch
   121	// and the remote-tracking ref as last fetched are scanned first; when both are
   122	// clean the answer is "OK" without a fetch, which keeps the routine doctor run
   123	// offline. When either shows a problem the tracking ref is refreshed and the
   124	// remote side re-scanned, so the fix that follows works from the remote's
   125	// current tip.
   126	func ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteName string, threshold int64) (*MetadataSizeScan, error) {
   127		v1 := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   128		scan := &MetadataSizeScan{Threshold: threshold, RemoteName: remoteName}
   129	
   130		localTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   131		if err != nil {
   132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   133		}
   134		scan.LocalTip = localTip
   135		scan.Local, err = findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, localTip, threshold)
   136		if err != nil {
   137			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   138		}

   140		// clone) is reported, not fatal: doctor's other checks must still run, and
   141		// with a clean local branch there is nothing this check would do anyway.
   142		var trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName
   143		var readErr error
   144		if remoteName != "" {
   145			trackingRef = plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, paths.MetadataBranchName)
   146			readErr = scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef)
   147		}

   149			scan.RemoteErr = readErr
   150			return scan, nil //nolint:nilerr // fail-soft: the unreadable tracking ref is reported on scan.RemoteErr, not fatal to doctor
   151		}
   152		// Something is oversized (or the stale tracking ref could not tell us).
   153		// Where pre-push actually sends the branch decides what happens next: a
   154		// dedicated checkpoint_remote URL has no remote-tracking ref to lease
   155		// against, and pre-push replays local commits onto whatever that URL
   156		// holds, so a local-only rewrite there would be undone by the next push.
   157		// Report it and stop rather than repair half of it — and decide that
   158		// BEFORE the no-remote early return below, so a repository whose only
   159		// checkpoint destination is the dedicated URL is refused the same way.
   160		// The settings are read directly rather than through resolvePushSettings,
   161		// which may fetch and create the local branch as a side effect; this scan
   162		// must stay read-only. They are read for THIS repository's worktree, not
   163		// the process working directory: the scan is handed a repo and must not
   164		// answer for whichever checkout the caller happens to be standing in.
   165		if s, loadErr := loadSettingsForRepo(ctx, repo); loadErr == nil {
   166			scan.PushDisabled = s.IsPushSessionsDisabled()
   167			if s.GetCheckpointRemote() != nil {
   168				scan.DedicatedCheckpointRemote = true
   169				scan.clearRemote()
   170				return scan, nil
   171			}
   172		} else {
   173			// Unknown push policy: do not push. The local rewrite is still useful.
   174			scan.PushDisabled = true
   175		}
   176		if remoteName == "" {
   177			return scan, nil
   178		}
   179		// Refresh from the remote so the fix works from its current tip.
   180		if fetchErr := refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx, remoteName, v1, trackingRef); fetchErr != nil {
   181			scan.RemoteErr = fetchErr
   182		}
   183		if err := scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef); err != nil {
   184			scan.RemoteErr = errors.Join(scan.RemoteErr, err)
   185			scan.clearRemote()
   186		}
   187		return scan, nil
   188	}
   189	
   190	// ErrDedicatedCheckpointRemote reports that the repository pushes its
   430	// messages, authors, dates and every other blob are preserved; commits whose
   431	// tree and parents are unchanged keep their hash, so history before the first
   432	// oversized blob is untouched.
   433	//
   434	// When the remote carries commits the local branch lacks (RemoteAhead), the
   435	// remote history is rewritten first and the local-only commits are replayed
   436	// onto it through SafelyAdvanceLocalRef — the same reconciliation pre-push
   437	// uses — so nothing either side holds is lost. The push is
   438	// --force-with-lease against the tip the scan observed, so a remote that moved
   439	// in between is refused rather than overwritten; re-running doctor rescans.
   440	//
   441	// On a push failure the returned result still describes the completed local
   442	// rewrite, so the caller can say what state the repository was left in.
   443	func ShrinkOversizedCheckpointMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, scan *MetadataSizeScan, w io.Writer) (*MetadataShrinkResult, error) {
   444		v1 := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   445		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   446		res := &MetadataShrinkResult{OldLocalTip: scan.LocalTip, NewLocalTip: scan.LocalTip}
   447		if scan.DedicatedCheckpointRemote {
   448			return res, ErrDedicatedCheckpointRemote
   449		}
   450		rw := newMetadataRewriter(ctx, repo, scan.Threshold)
   451	
   452		// Local first. When the remote is ahead, its history is rewritten with the
   453		// same memoized rewriter, so every commit the two sides share maps to the
   454		// same rewritten commit and the rewritten local tip is an ancestor of the
   455		// rewritten remote tip (or shares its rewritten merge base). Reconciling
   456		// the ORIGINAL local tip against a rewritten remote would find no common
   457		// history past the first oversized blob and replay every commit since as
   458		// a duplicate.
   459		newTip, err := rw.rewriteHistory(scan.LocalTip)
   460		if err != nil {
   461			return res, fmt.Errorf("rewrite %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   462		}
   463		res.CommitsRewritten = rw.commitsRewritten
   464		if !newTip.Equal(scan.LocalTip) {
   465			if err := atomicSetV1Ref(ctx, repo, scan.LocalTip, newTip); err != nil {
   466				return res, err
   467			}
   468			res.NewLocalTip = newTip
   469		}
   470	
   471		if !scan.RemoteTip.IsZero() && scan.RemoteAhead {
   472			before := rw.commitsRewritten
   473			fixedRemote, err := rw.rewriteHistory(scan.RemoteTip)
   474			if err != nil {
   475				return res, fmt.Errorf("rewrite %s/%s: %w", scan.RemoteName, v1.Short(), err)
   476			}
   477			res.RemoteCommitsRewritten = rw.commitsRewritten - before
   478			newTip, err = reconcileRewrittenTips(ctx, repo, w, scan.RemoteName, v1, newTip, fixedRemote)
   479			if err != nil {
   480				return res, err
   481			}
   482			res.NewLocalTip = newTip
   483		}
   484		res.BlobsShrunk = rw.blobsShrunk
   485		res.StillOversized = rw.stillOversized
   486		logging.Info(logCtx, "shrank oversized checkpoint metadata",
   487			slog.String("old_tip", scan.LocalTip.String()),
   488			slog.String("new_tip", newTip.String()),
   489			slog.Int("commits_rewritten", res.CommitsRewritten),
   490			slog.Int("remote_commits_rewritten", res.RemoteCommitsRewritten),
   491			slog.Int("blobs_shrunk", rw.blobsShrunk))
   492	
   493		switch {
   494		case scan.RemoteName == "":
   495			res.PushSkippedReason = "no checkpoint sync remote is configured"
   496		case scan.RemoteTip.IsZero() && scan.RemoteErr != nil:
   497			res.PushSkippedReason = fmt.Sprintf("the state of %s could not be determined (%v); re-run entire doctor once it is reachable", scan.RemoteName, scan.RemoteErr)
   498		case scan.RemoteTip.IsZero():
   499			res.PushSkippedReason = fmt.Sprintf("%s has no %s branch yet; the next git push creates it", scan.RemoteName, v1.Short())
   500		case scan.RemoteTip.Equal(newTip):
   501			res.PushSkippedReason = scan.RemoteName + " already has this history"
   502		case scan.PushDisabled:
   503			res.PushSkippedReason = "checkpoint pushing is disabled in settings; push the branch yourself with --force-with-lease"
   504		default:
   505			if err := forcePushCheckpointBranch(ctx, scan.RemoteName, v1, scan.RemoteTip, newTip); err != nil {
   506				return res, &PushFailedError{Remote: scan.RemoteName, Err: err}
   507			}
   508			res.Pushed = true
   509		}
   510		return res, nil
   511	}
   512	
   513	// reconcileRewrittenTips brings the local branch (at rewritten tip local) and
   514	// the rewritten remote history (fixedRemote) together and returns the new
   515	// local tip. Three cases, decided on content rather than hashes because
   516	// independent rewrites of the same history differ in hash when commit signing
   517	// is on:
   518	//
   519	//   - the remote already holds everything local has (local's tree appears in
   520	//     the remote's history): adopt the remote tip, no replay;
   521	//   - local already holds everything the remote has: keep local, which the
   522	//     caller then pushes;
   523	//   - genuine divergence: replay the local-only commits onto the remote via
   524	//     SafelyAdvanceLocalRef, the same reconciliation pre-push uses.
   525	func reconcileRewrittenTips(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, w io.Writer, remoteName string, v1 plumbing.ReferenceName, local, fixedRemote plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   526		if fixedRemote.Equal(local) {
   527			return local, nil
   528		}
   529		if local.IsZero() {
   530			if err := SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, v1, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   531				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("adopt %s/%s: %w", remoteName, v1.Short(), err)
   532			}
   533			return fixedRemote, nil
   534		}
   535		remoteHasLocal, err := contentReachable(repo, fixedRemote, local)
   536		if err != nil {
   537			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   538		}
   539		if remoteHasLocal {
   540			fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Remote %s already holds every local checkpoint; adopting its history.\n", remoteName)
   541			if err := atomicSetV1Ref(ctx, repo, local, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   542				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   543			}
   544			return fixedRemote, nil
   545		}
   546		localHasRemote, err := contentReachable(repo, local, fixedRemote)
   547		if err != nil {
   548			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   549		}
   550		if localHasRemote {
   551			return local, nil
   552		}
   553		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Remote %s has checkpoints not yet local; replaying local checkpoints onto it.\n", remoteName)
   554		if err := SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, v1, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   555			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("reconcile local %s with %s: %w", v1.Short(), remoteName, err)
   556		}
   557		tip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   558		if err != nil {
   559			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("re-read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   560		}
   561		return tip, nil
   562	}
   563	
   564	// forcePushCheckpointBranch replaces the remote's checkpoint branch with newTip,
   565	// refusing (via --force-with-lease) if the remote no longer sits at expected.
   566	func forcePushCheckpointBranch(ctx context.Context, remoteName string, branch plumbing.ReferenceName, expected, newTip plumbing.Hash) error {
   567		pushCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
   568		defer cancel()
   569		_, err := remote.PushWithOptions(pushCtx, remote.PushOptions{
   570			Remote:    remoteName,
   571			RefSpecs:  []string{newTip.String() + ":" + branch.String()},
   572			ExtraArgs: []string{"--force-with-lease=" + branch.String() + ":" + expected.String()},
   573		})
   574		if err != nil {
   575			return fmt.Errorf("force-push %s to %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, err)
   576		}
   577		return nil
   578	}
   579	
   580	// metadataRewriter rewrites a commit graph replacing oversized metadata.json
   581	// blobs. Every level is memoized: a blob is stripped once however many trees
   582	// reference it, a tree is rebuilt once however many commits share it, and a
   583	// commit is rewritten once however many children it has.
   584	type metadataRewriter struct {
   585		ctx       context.Context //nolint:containedctx // scoped to one rewrite; threaded into commit signing
   586		repo      *git.Repository
   587		threshold int64
   588	
   589		blobs   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   590		trees   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   598	func newMetadataRewriter(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, threshold int64) *metadataRewriter {
   599		return &metadataRewriter{
   600			ctx:       ctx,
   601			repo:      repo,
   602			threshold: threshold,
   603			blobs:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   604			trees:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   605			commits:   make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   606		}
   607	}
   608	
   609	// rewriteHistory returns the rewritten equivalent of tip. Parents are processed
   610	// before children with an explicit stack, so a branch with thousands of
   611	// checkpoints does not recurse thousands deep.
   612	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteHistory(tip plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   613		if tip.IsZero() {
   614			return tip, nil
   615		}
   616		type frame struct {
   617			hash     plumbing.Hash
   618			expanded bool
   619		}
   620		stack := []frame{{hash: tip}}
   621		for len(stack) > 0 {
   622			if err := r.ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   623				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err //nolint:wrapcheck // context cancellation propagates as-is
   624			}
   625			top := len(stack) - 1
   626			f := stack[top]
   627			if _, done := r.commits[f.hash]; done {
   628				stack = stack[:top]
   629				continue
   630			}
   631			c, err := r.repo.CommitObject(f.hash)
   632			if err != nil {
   633				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load commit %s: %w", f.hash, err)
   634			}
   635			if !f.expanded {
   636				stack[top].expanded = true
   637				for _, p := range c.ParentHashes {
   638					if _, done := r.commits[p]; !done {
   639						stack = append(stack, frame{hash: p})
   640					}
   641				}
   642				continue
   643			}
   644			newHash, err := r.rewriteCommit(c)
   645			if err != nil {
   646				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   647			}
   648			r.commits[f.hash] = newHash
   649			stack = stack[:top]
   650		}
   651		return r.commits[tip], nil
   652	}
   653	
   654	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteCommit(c *object.Commit) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   655		newTree, err := r.rewriteTree(c.TreeHash, "")
   656		if err != nil {
   657			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   658		}
   659		parents := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(c.ParentHashes))
   660		changed := !newTree.Equal(c.TreeHash)
   661		for _, p := range c.ParentHashes {
   662			np, ok := r.commits[p]
   663			if !ok {
   664				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("parent %s of %s was not rewritten first", p, c.Hash)
   665			}
   666			if !np.Equal(p) {
   667				changed = true
   668			}
   669			parents = append(parents, np)
   670		}
   671		if !changed {
   672			return c.Hash, nil
   673		}
   674		rewritten := &object.Commit{
   675			Author:       c.Author,
   676			Committer:    c.Committer,
   677			Message:      c.Message,
   678			TreeHash:     newTree,
   679			ParentHashes: parents,
   680			Encoding:     c.Encoding,
   681			ExtraHeaders: c.ExtraHeaders,
   682		}
   683		// Re-sign when signing is configured: the original signature covered the
   684		// original tree, so it cannot be carried over. Signing makes the rewritten
   685		// hash non-deterministic across runs, which is why reconciliation below
   686		// compares trees (contentReachable) rather than hashes.
   687		checkpoint.SignCommitBestEffort(r.ctx, rewritten)
   688		obj := r.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   689		if err := rewritten.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   690			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode rewritten commit %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   691		}
   692		hash, err := r.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   693		if err != nil {
   694			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store rewritten commit %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   695		}
   696		r.commitsRewritten++
   697		return hash, nil
   698	}
   699	
   700	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteTree(hash plumbing.Hash, prefix string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   701		if done, ok := r.trees[hash]; ok {
   702			return done, nil
   703		}
   704		tree, err := r.repo.TreeObject(hash)
   705		if err != nil {
   706			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load tree %s: %w", hash, err)
   707		}
   708		entries := make([]object.TreeEntry, 0, len(tree.Entries))
   709		changed := false
   710		for _, e := range tree.Entries {
   711			entryPath := e.Name
   712			if prefix != "" {
   713				entryPath = prefix + "/" + e.Name
   714			}
   715			newEntry := e
   716			switch e.Mode {
   717			case filemode.Dir:
   718				sub, subErr := r.rewriteTree(e.Hash, entryPath)
   719				if subErr != nil {
   720					return plumbing.ZeroHash, subErr
   721				}
   722				newEntry.Hash = sub
   723			case filemode.Regular, filemode.Executable, filemode.Deprecated:
   724				if e.Name == paths.MetadataFileName {
   725					blob, blobErr := r.rewriteBlob(e.Hash, entryPath)
   726					if blobErr != nil {
   727						return plumbing.ZeroHash, blobErr
   728					}
   729					newEntry.Hash = blob
   730				}
   731			case filemode.Empty, filemode.Symlink, filemode.Submodule:
   732				// kept verbatim
   733			}
   734			if !newEntry.Hash.Equal(e.Hash) {
   735				changed = true
   736			}
   737			entries = append(entries, newEntry)
   738		}
   739		if !changed {
   740			r.trees[hash] = hash
   741			return hash, nil
   742		}
   743		newTree := &object.Tree{Entries: entries}
   744		obj := r.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   745		if err := newTree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   746			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode tree %s: %w", prefix, err)
   747		}
   748		newHash, err := r.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   749		if err != nil {
   750			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store tree %s: %w", prefix, err)
   751		}
   752		r.trees[hash] = newHash
   753		return newHash, nil
   754	}
   755	
   756	// rewriteBlob returns the replacement for a metadata.json blob: itself when it
   757	// is under the threshold or carries no prompt_attributions, else a copy without
   758	// that field.
   759	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteBlob(hash plumbing.Hash, blobPath string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   760		if done, ok := r.blobs[hash]; ok {
   761			return done, nil
   762		}
   763		blob, err := r.repo.BlobObject(hash)
   764		if err != nil {
   765			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, err)
   766		}
   767		if blob.Size <= r.threshold {
   768			r.blobs[hash] = hash
   769			return hash, nil
   770		}
   771		data, err := readBlob(r.repo, hash)
   772		if err != nil {
   773			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("read blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, err)
   774		}
   775		stripped, changed, err := stripPromptAttributions(data)
   776		if err != nil || !changed {
   777			// Either not the JSON this repair understands, or large for a reason
   778			// other than the field it knows how to remove: leave it and say so
   779			// rather than guess at what to delete.
   780			r.stillOversized = append(r.stillOversized, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: blob.Size, Hash: hash})
   781			r.blobs[hash] = hash
   782			return hash, nil //nolint:nilerr // deliberate: an unparseable blob is kept verbatim and reported via stillOversized
   783		}
   784		newHash, err := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(r.repo, stripped)
   785		if err != nil {
   786			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("write shrunk blob for %s: %w", blobPath, err)
   787		}
   788		r.blobsShrunk++
   789		if int64(len(stripped)) > r.threshold {
   790			r.stillOversized = append(r.stillOversized, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: int64(len(stripped)), Hash: newHash})
   791		}
   792		r.blobs[hash] = newHash
   793		return newHash, nil
   794	}
   795	
   796	// stripPromptAttributions removes the prompt_attributions key from a
   797	// metadata.json document, preserving every other field verbatim (as raw JSON),
   798	// and reports whether anything changed. Keys come back sorted, which is the one
   799	// cosmetic difference from the writer's field order.
   800	func stripPromptAttributions(data []byte) ([]byte, bool, error) {
   801		var doc map[string]json.RawMessage
   802		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &doc); err != nil {
   803			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("parse metadata.json: %w", err)
   804		}
   805		if _, ok := doc[promptAttributionsField]; !ok {
   806			return data, false, nil
   807		}
   808		delete(doc, promptAttributionsField)
   809		out, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(doc, "", "  ")
   810		if err != nil {
   811			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("re-encode metadata.json: %w", err)
   812		}
   813		return out, true, nil
   814	}

    27	// OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold is the blob size above which a
    28	// per-session metadata.json on entire/checkpoints/v1 is reported by
    29	// `entire doctor`. GitHub warns at 50 MiB and refuses any blob over 100 MiB, and
    30	// a refused blob anywhere in the branch's history makes the whole branch
    31	// unpushable there — including through a forge's push mirror. A healthy
    32	// metadata.json is tens of kilobytes, so anything past this line is the
    33	// pre-v0.10.1 prompt_attributions bloat (see checkpoint.MaxPromptAttributionsBytes),
    34	// not a large session.
    35	const OversizedCheckpointMetadataThreshold int64 = 50 << 20
    36	
    37	// promptAttributionsField is the metadata.json key the shrink removes. It is
    38	// the only field whose size scales with the working tree rather than the
    39	// session, and nothing reads it back — the attribution summary it fed is a
    40	// separate field that stays.
    41	const promptAttributionsField = "prompt_attributions"
    42	
    43	// OversizedMetadataBlob is one metadata.json blob over the threshold.
    44	type OversizedMetadataBlob struct {
    45		Path   string        // tree path, e.g. "ab/cdef.../0/metadata.json"
    46		Size   int64         // blob size in bytes
    47		Hash   plumbing.Hash // blob hash
    48		Commit plumbing.Hash // the commit that introduced this blob version
    49	}
    50	
    51	// MetadataSizeScan is the read-only half of the oversized-metadata repair: what
    52	// is oversized, where, and what the elected sync remote holds, so the report and
    53	// the fix share one fetch.
    54	type MetadataSizeScan struct {
    55		Threshold  int64
    56		LocalTip   plumbing.Hash // zero when the branch does not exist locally
    57		RemoteName string        // elected checkpoint sync remote; "" when none
    58		// RemoteTip is the remote-tracking tip of the checkpoint branch on
    59		// RemoteName after a refresh. Zero when there is no remote, the remote has
    60		// no such branch, or the refresh failed and no stale tracking ref exists.
    61		RemoteTip plumbing.Hash
    62		// RemoteErr records a failed refresh or an unreadable tracking ref. After a
    63		// failed refresh RemoteTip may still reflect the tracking ref as it was,
    64		// which the force-with-lease push guards against; after an unreadable ref
    65		// the remote fields are cleared and the fix does not push.
    66		RemoteErr error
    67		// RemoteAhead reports that RemoteTip carries commits LocalTip does not.
    68		RemoteAhead  bool
    69		PushDisabled bool
    70		// DedicatedCheckpointRemote reports that the branch is pushed to a
    71		// checkpoint_remote URL rather than to RemoteName; the fix is withheld.
    72		DedicatedCheckpointRemote bool
    73		// Local are oversized blobs reachable from LocalTip; Remote those reachable
    74		// from RemoteTip and not already in Local.
    75		Local  []OversizedMetadataBlob
    76		Remote []OversizedMetadataBlob
    77	}
    78	
    79	// Empty reports whether nothing is oversized on either side.
    80	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) Empty() bool { return len(s.Local) == 0 && len(s.Remote) == 0 }

    82	// All returns every oversized blob, largest first.
    83	func (s *MetadataSizeScan) All() []OversizedMetadataBlob {
    84		all := make([]OversizedMetadataBlob, 0, len(s.Local)+len(s.Remote))
    85		all = append(all, s.Local...)
    86		all = append(all, s.Remote...)
    87		sort.SliceStable(all, func(i, j int) bool { return all[i].Size > all[j].Size })
    88		return all
    89	}

    91	// MetadataShrinkResult describes what ShrinkOversizedCheckpointMetadata did.
    92	type MetadataShrinkResult struct {
    93		OldLocalTip plumbing.Hash
    94		NewLocalTip plumbing.Hash
    95		// CommitsRewritten counts commits of the local branch that were rebuilt.
    96		CommitsRewritten int
    97		// RemoteCommitsRewritten counts commits of the remote's history that were
    98		// rebuilt because the remote was ahead of the local branch.
    99		RemoteCommitsRewritten int
   100		BlobsShrunk            int
   101		// StillOversized lists blobs that remain over the threshold after the
   102		// prompt_attributions field was removed — bloat of a kind this repair does
   103		// not know about, reported rather than guessed at.
   104		StillOversized []OversizedMetadataBlob
   105		Pushed         bool
   106		// PushSkippedReason explains a Pushed == false when no error occurred.
   107		PushSkippedReason string
   108	}
   109	
   110	// ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata refreshes the elected sync remote's tracking
   111	// ref for the checkpoint branch (best effort) and reports every metadata.json
   112	// blob over threshold reachable from the local branch or from that tracking ref.
   113	// It is read-only: nothing under refs/heads is touched.
   114	//
   115	// The remote side matters because the repair force-pushes: a blob that is only
   116	// on the remote (an earlier local repair whose push failed) still blocks the
   117	// mirror, and an ordinary pre-push would replay the local branch onto that
   118	// remote history and reintroduce it.
   119	//
   120	// The network is touched only when something is oversized. The local branch
   121	// and the remote-tracking ref as last fetched are scanned first; when both are
   122	// clean the answer is "OK" without a fetch, which keeps the routine doctor run
   123	// offline. When either shows a problem the tracking ref is refreshed and the
   124	// remote side re-scanned, so the fix that follows works from the remote's
   125	// current tip.
   126	func ScanOversizedCheckpointMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remoteName string, threshold int64) (*MetadataSizeScan, error) {
   127		v1 := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   128		scan := &MetadataSizeScan{Threshold: threshold, RemoteName: remoteName}
   129	
   130		localTip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   131		if err != nil {
   132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   133		}
   134		scan.LocalTip = localTip
   135		scan.Local, err = findOversizedMetadataBlobs(ctx, repo, localTip, threshold)
   136		if err != nil {
   137			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scan local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   138		}
   139		// The tracking ref as last fetched. An unreadable one (dangling, partial
   140		// clone) is reported, not fatal: doctor's other checks must still run, and
   141		// with a clean local branch there is nothing this check would do anyway.
   142		var trackingRef plumbing.ReferenceName
   143		var readErr error
   144		if remoteName != "" {
   145			trackingRef = plumbing.NewRemoteReferenceName(remoteName, paths.MetadataBranchName)
   146			readErr = scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef)
   147		}
   148		if len(scan.Local) == 0 && (remoteName == "" || readErr != nil || len(scan.Remote) == 0) {
   149			scan.RemoteErr = readErr
   150			return scan, nil //nolint:nilerr // fail-soft: the unreadable tracking ref is reported on scan.RemoteErr, not fatal to doctor
   151		}
   152		// Something is oversized (or the stale tracking ref could not tell us).
   153		// Where pre-push actually sends the branch decides what happens next: a
   154		// dedicated checkpoint_remote URL has no remote-tracking ref to lease
   155		// against, and pre-push replays local commits onto whatever that URL
   156		// holds, so a local-only rewrite there would be undone by the next push.
   157		// Report it and stop rather than repair half of it — and decide that
   158		// BEFORE the no-remote early return below, so a repository whose only
   159		// checkpoint destination is the dedicated URL is refused the same way.
   160		// The settings are read directly rather than through resolvePushSettings,
   161		// which may fetch and create the local branch as a side effect; this scan
   162		// must stay read-only. They are read for THIS repository's worktree, not
   163		// the process working directory: the scan is handed a repo and must not
   164		// answer for whichever checkout the caller happens to be standing in.
   165		if s, loadErr := loadSettingsForRepo(ctx, repo); loadErr == nil {
   166			scan.PushDisabled = s.IsPushSessionsDisabled()
   167			if s.GetCheckpointRemote() != nil {
   168				scan.DedicatedCheckpointRemote = true
   169				scan.clearRemote()
   170				return scan, nil
   171			}
   172		} else {
   173			// Unknown push policy: do not push. The local rewrite is still useful.
   174			scan.PushDisabled = true
   175		}
   176		if remoteName == "" {
   177			return scan, nil
   178		}
   179		// Refresh from the remote so the fix works from its current tip.
   180		if fetchErr := refreshCheckpointTrackingRef(ctx, remoteName, v1, trackingRef); fetchErr != nil {
   181			scan.RemoteErr = fetchErr
   182		}
   183		if err := scan.readRemoteSide(ctx, repo, trackingRef); err != nil {
   184			scan.RemoteErr = errors.Join(scan.RemoteErr, err)
   185			scan.clearRemote()
   186		}
   187		return scan, nil
   188	}
   189	
   190	// ErrDedicatedCheckpointRemote reports that the repository pushes its
   430	// messages, authors, dates and every other blob are preserved; commits whose
   431	// tree and parents are unchanged keep their hash, so history before the first
   432	// oversized blob is untouched.
   433	//
   434	// When the remote carries commits the local branch lacks (RemoteAhead), the
   435	// remote history is rewritten first and the local-only commits are replayed
   436	// onto it through SafelyAdvanceLocalRef — the same reconciliation pre-push
   437	// uses — so nothing either side holds is lost. The push is
   438	// --force-with-lease against the tip the scan observed, so a remote that moved
   439	// in between is refused rather than overwritten; re-running doctor rescans.
   440	//
   441	// On a push failure the returned result still describes the completed local
   442	// rewrite, so the caller can say what state the repository was left in.
   443	func ShrinkOversizedCheckpointMetadata(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, scan *MetadataSizeScan, w io.Writer) (*MetadataShrinkResult, error) {
   444		v1 := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
   445		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   446		res := &MetadataShrinkResult{OldLocalTip: scan.LocalTip, NewLocalTip: scan.LocalTip}
   447		if scan.DedicatedCheckpointRemote {
   448			return res, ErrDedicatedCheckpointRemote
   449		}
   450		rw := newMetadataRewriter(ctx, repo, scan.Threshold)
   451	
   452		// Local first. When the remote is ahead, its history is rewritten with the
   453		// same memoized rewriter, so every commit the two sides share maps to the
   454		// same rewritten commit and the rewritten local tip is an ancestor of the
   455		// rewritten remote tip (or shares its rewritten merge base). Reconciling
   456		// the ORIGINAL local tip against a rewritten remote would find no common
   457		// history past the first oversized blob and replay every commit since as
   458		// a duplicate.
   459		newTip, err := rw.rewriteHistory(scan.LocalTip)
   460		if err != nil {
   461			return res, fmt.Errorf("rewrite %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   462		}
   463		res.CommitsRewritten = rw.commitsRewritten
   464		if !newTip.Equal(scan.LocalTip) {
   465			if err := atomicSetV1Ref(ctx, repo, scan.LocalTip, newTip); err != nil {
   466				return res, err
   467			}
   468			res.NewLocalTip = newTip
   469		}
   470	
   471		if !scan.RemoteTip.IsZero() && scan.RemoteAhead {
   472			before := rw.commitsRewritten
   473			fixedRemote, err := rw.rewriteHistory(scan.RemoteTip)
   474			if err != nil {
   475				return res, fmt.Errorf("rewrite %s/%s: %w", scan.RemoteName, v1.Short(), err)
   476			}
   477			res.RemoteCommitsRewritten = rw.commitsRewritten - before
   478			newTip, err = reconcileRewrittenTips(ctx, repo, w, scan.RemoteName, v1, newTip, fixedRemote)
   479			if err != nil {
   480				return res, err
   481			}
   482			res.NewLocalTip = newTip
   483		}
   484		res.BlobsShrunk = rw.blobsShrunk
   485		res.StillOversized = rw.stillOversized
   486		logging.Info(logCtx, "shrank oversized checkpoint metadata",
   487			slog.String("old_tip", scan.LocalTip.String()),
   488			slog.String("new_tip", newTip.String()),
   489			slog.Int("commits_rewritten", res.CommitsRewritten),
   490			slog.Int("remote_commits_rewritten", res.RemoteCommitsRewritten),
   491			slog.Int("blobs_shrunk", rw.blobsShrunk))
   492	
   493		switch {
   494		case scan.RemoteName == "":
   495			res.PushSkippedReason = "no checkpoint sync remote is configured"
   496		case scan.RemoteTip.IsZero() && scan.RemoteErr != nil:
   497			res.PushSkippedReason = fmt.Sprintf("the state of %s could not be determined (%v); re-run entire doctor once it is reachable", scan.RemoteName, scan.RemoteErr)
   498		case scan.RemoteTip.IsZero():
   499			res.PushSkippedReason = fmt.Sprintf("%s has no %s branch yet; the next git push creates it", scan.RemoteName, v1.Short())
   500		case scan.RemoteTip.Equal(newTip):
   501			res.PushSkippedReason = scan.RemoteName + " already has this history"
   502		case scan.PushDisabled:
   503			res.PushSkippedReason = "checkpoint pushing is disabled in settings; push the branch yourself with --force-with-lease"
   504		default:
   505			if err := forcePushCheckpointBranch(ctx, scan.RemoteName, v1, scan.RemoteTip, newTip); err != nil {
   506				return res, &PushFailedError{Remote: scan.RemoteName, Err: err}
   507			}
   508			res.Pushed = true
   509		}
   510		return res, nil
   511	}
   512	
   513	// reconcileRewrittenTips brings the local branch (at rewritten tip local) and
   514	// the rewritten remote history (fixedRemote) together and returns the new
   515	// local tip. Three cases, decided on content rather than hashes because
   516	// independent rewrites of the same history differ in hash when commit signing
   517	// is on:
   518	//
   519	//   - the remote already holds everything local has (local's tree appears in
   520	//     the remote's history): adopt the remote tip, no replay;
   521	//   - local already holds everything the remote has: keep local, which the
   522	//     caller then pushes;
   523	//   - genuine divergence: replay the local-only commits onto the remote via
   524	//     SafelyAdvanceLocalRef, the same reconciliation pre-push uses.
   525	func reconcileRewrittenTips(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, w io.Writer, remoteName string, v1 plumbing.ReferenceName, local, fixedRemote plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   526		if fixedRemote.Equal(local) {
   527			return local, nil
   528		}
   529		if local.IsZero() {
   530			if err := SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, v1, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   531				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("adopt %s/%s: %w", remoteName, v1.Short(), err)
   532			}
   533			return fixedRemote, nil
   534		}
   535		remoteHasLocal, err := contentReachable(repo, fixedRemote, local)
   536		if err != nil {
   537			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   538		}
   539		if remoteHasLocal {
   540			fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Remote %s already holds every local checkpoint; adopting its history.\n", remoteName)
   541			if err := atomicSetV1Ref(ctx, repo, local, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   542				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   543			}
   544			return fixedRemote, nil
   545		}
   546		localHasRemote, err := contentReachable(repo, local, fixedRemote)
   547		if err != nil {
   548			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   549		}
   550		if localHasRemote {
   551			return local, nil
   552		}
   553		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Remote %s has checkpoints not yet local; replaying local checkpoints onto it.\n", remoteName)
   554		if err := SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, v1, fixedRemote); err != nil {
   555			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("reconcile local %s with %s: %w", v1.Short(), remoteName, err)
   556		}
   557		tip, err := readV1Tip(repo, v1)
   558		if err != nil {
   559			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("re-read local %s: %w", v1.Short(), err)
   560		}
   561		return tip, nil
   562	}

   564	// forcePushCheckpointBranch replaces the remote's checkpoint branch with newTip,
   565	// refusing (via --force-with-lease) if the remote no longer sits at expected.
   566	func forcePushCheckpointBranch(ctx context.Context, remoteName string, branch plumbing.ReferenceName, expected, newTip plumbing.Hash) error {
   567		pushCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
   568		defer cancel()
   569		_, err := remote.PushWithOptions(pushCtx, remote.PushOptions{
   570			Remote:    remoteName,
   571			RefSpecs:  []string{newTip.String() + ":" + branch.String()},
   572			ExtraArgs: []string{"--force-with-lease=" + branch.String() + ":" + expected.String()},
   573		})
   574		if err != nil {
   575			return fmt.Errorf("force-push %s to %s: %w", branch.Short(), remoteName, err)
   576		}
   577		return nil
   578	}

   580	// metadataRewriter rewrites a commit graph replacing oversized metadata.json
   581	// blobs. Every level is memoized: a blob is stripped once however many trees
   582	// reference it, a tree is rebuilt once however many commits share it, and a
   583	// commit is rewritten once however many children it has.
   584	type metadataRewriter struct {
   585		ctx       context.Context //nolint:containedctx // scoped to one rewrite; threaded into commit signing
   586		repo      *git.Repository
   587		threshold int64
   588	
   589		blobs   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   590		trees   map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash
   598	func newMetadataRewriter(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, threshold int64) *metadataRewriter {
   599		return &metadataRewriter{
   600			ctx:       ctx,
   601			repo:      repo,
   602			threshold: threshold,
   603			blobs:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   604			trees:     make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   605			commits:   make(map[plumbing.Hash]plumbing.Hash),
   606		}
   607	}
   608	
   609	// rewriteHistory returns the rewritten equivalent of tip. Parents are processed
   610	// before children with an explicit stack, so a branch with thousands of
   611	// checkpoints does not recurse thousands deep.
   612	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteHistory(tip plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   613		if tip.IsZero() {
   614			return tip, nil
   615		}
   616		type frame struct {
   617			hash     plumbing.Hash
   618			expanded bool
   619		}
   620		stack := []frame{{hash: tip}}
   621		for len(stack) > 0 {
   622			if err := r.ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   623				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err //nolint:wrapcheck // context cancellation propagates as-is
   624			}
   625			top := len(stack) - 1
   626			f := stack[top]
   627			if _, done := r.commits[f.hash]; done {
   628				stack = stack[:top]
   629				continue
   630			}
   631			c, err := r.repo.CommitObject(f.hash)
   632			if err != nil {
   633				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load commit %s: %w", f.hash, err)
   634			}
   635			if !f.expanded {
   636				stack[top].expanded = true
   637				for _, p := range c.ParentHashes {
   638					if _, done := r.commits[p]; !done {
   639						stack = append(stack, frame{hash: p})
   640					}
   641				}
   642				continue
   643			}
   644			newHash, err := r.rewriteCommit(c)
   645			if err != nil {
   646				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   647			}
   648			r.commits[f.hash] = newHash
   649			stack = stack[:top]
   650		}
   651		return r.commits[tip], nil
   652	}
   653	
   654	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteCommit(c *object.Commit) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   655		newTree, err := r.rewriteTree(c.TreeHash, "")
   656		if err != nil {
   657			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   658		}
   659		parents := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(c.ParentHashes))
   660		changed := !newTree.Equal(c.TreeHash)
   661		for _, p := range c.ParentHashes {
   662			np, ok := r.commits[p]
   663			if !ok {
   664				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("parent %s of %s was not rewritten first", p, c.Hash)
   665			}
   666			if !np.Equal(p) {
   667				changed = true
   668			}
   669			parents = append(parents, np)
   670		}
   671		if !changed {
   672			return c.Hash, nil
   673		}
   674		rewritten := &object.Commit{
   675			Author:       c.Author,
   676			Committer:    c.Committer,
   677			Message:      c.Message,
   678			TreeHash:     newTree,
   679			ParentHashes: parents,
   680			Encoding:     c.Encoding,
   681			ExtraHeaders: c.ExtraHeaders,
   682		}
   683		// Re-sign when signing is configured: the original signature covered the
   684		// original tree, so it cannot be carried over. Signing makes the rewritten
   685		// hash non-deterministic across runs, which is why reconciliation below
   686		// compares trees (contentReachable) rather than hashes.
   687		checkpoint.SignCommitBestEffort(r.ctx, rewritten)
   688		obj := r.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   689		if err := rewritten.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   690			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode rewritten commit %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   691		}
   692		hash, err := r.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   693		if err != nil {
   694			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store rewritten commit %s: %w", c.Hash, err)
   695		}
   696		r.commitsRewritten++
   697		return hash, nil
   698	}
   699	
   700	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteTree(hash plumbing.Hash, prefix string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   701		if done, ok := r.trees[hash]; ok {
   702			return done, nil
   703		}
   704		tree, err := r.repo.TreeObject(hash)
   705		if err != nil {
   706			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load tree %s: %w", hash, err)
   707		}
   708		entries := make([]object.TreeEntry, 0, len(tree.Entries))
   709		changed := false
   710		for _, e := range tree.Entries {
   711			entryPath := e.Name
   712			if prefix != "" {
   713				entryPath = prefix + "/" + e.Name
   714			}
   715			newEntry := e
   716			switch e.Mode {
   717			case filemode.Dir:
   718				sub, subErr := r.rewriteTree(e.Hash, entryPath)
   719				if subErr != nil {
   720					return plumbing.ZeroHash, subErr
   721				}
   722				newEntry.Hash = sub
   723			case filemode.Regular, filemode.Executable, filemode.Deprecated:
   724				if e.Name == paths.MetadataFileName {
   725					blob, blobErr := r.rewriteBlob(e.Hash, entryPath)
   726					if blobErr != nil {
   727						return plumbing.ZeroHash, blobErr
   728					}
   729					newEntry.Hash = blob
   730				}
   731			case filemode.Empty, filemode.Symlink, filemode.Submodule:
   732				// kept verbatim
   733			}
   734			if !newEntry.Hash.Equal(e.Hash) {
   735				changed = true
   736			}
   737			entries = append(entries, newEntry)
   738		}
   739		if !changed {
   740			r.trees[hash] = hash
   741			return hash, nil
   742		}
   743		newTree := &object.Tree{Entries: entries}
   744		obj := r.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   745		if err := newTree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   746			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode tree %s: %w", prefix, err)
   747		}
   748		newHash, err := r.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   749		if err != nil {
   750			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store tree %s: %w", prefix, err)
   751		}
   752		r.trees[hash] = newHash
   753		return newHash, nil
   754	}
   755	
   756	// rewriteBlob returns the replacement for a metadata.json blob: itself when it
   757	// is under the threshold or carries no prompt_attributions, else a copy without
   758	// that field.
   759	func (r *metadataRewriter) rewriteBlob(hash plumbing.Hash, blobPath string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   760		if done, ok := r.blobs[hash]; ok {
   761			return done, nil
   762		}
   763		blob, err := r.repo.BlobObject(hash)
   764		if err != nil {
   765			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, err)
   766		}
   767		if blob.Size <= r.threshold {
   768			r.blobs[hash] = hash
   769			return hash, nil
   770		}
   771		data, err := readBlob(r.repo, hash)
   772		if err != nil {
   773			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("read blob %s at %s: %w", hash, blobPath, err)
   774		}
   775		stripped, changed, err := stripPromptAttributions(data)
   776		if err != nil || !changed {
   777			// Either not the JSON this repair understands, or large for a reason
   778			// other than the field it knows how to remove: leave it and say so
   779			// rather than guess at what to delete.
   780			r.stillOversized = append(r.stillOversized, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: blob.Size, Hash: hash})
   781			r.blobs[hash] = hash
   782			return hash, nil //nolint:nilerr // deliberate: an unparseable blob is kept verbatim and reported via stillOversized
   783		}
   784		newHash, err := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(r.repo, stripped)
   785		if err != nil {
   786			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("write shrunk blob for %s: %w", blobPath, err)
   787		}
   788		r.blobsShrunk++
   789		if int64(len(stripped)) > r.threshold {
   790			r.stillOversized = append(r.stillOversized, OversizedMetadataBlob{Path: blobPath, Size: int64(len(stripped)), Hash: newHash})
   791		}
   792		r.blobs[hash] = newHash
   793		return newHash, nil
   794	}
   795	
   796	// stripPromptAttributions removes the prompt_attributions key from a
   797	// metadata.json document, preserving every other field verbatim (as raw JSON),
   798	// and reports whether anything changed. Keys come back sorted, which is the one
   799	// cosmetic difference from the writer's field order.
   800	func stripPromptAttributions(data []byte) ([]byte, bool, error) {
   801		var doc map[string]json.RawMessage
   802		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &doc); err != nil {
   803			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("parse metadata.json: %w", err)
   804		}
   805		if _, ok := doc[promptAttributionsField]; !ok {
   806			return data, false, nil
   807		}
   808		delete(doc, promptAttributionsField)
   809		out, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(doc, "", "  ")
   810		if err != nil {
   811			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("re-encode metadata.json: %w", err)
   812		}
   813		return out, true, nil
   814	}

   236	// Outside a git repository there is no worktree root and so nothing to
   237	// validate, which is not an error: commands that need a repository report its

   101	// claudeHookConfig returns .claude/settings.json for the current worktree,
   102	// opened through the worktree's root. Every read, write and removal of that
   103	// file goes through it: the path lives in the working tree, which arrives by
   104	// clone, so a checked-in symlink at `.claude` must not be a directory Entire
   105	// creates and writes through.
   106	func claudeHookConfig(ctx context.Context) (*agent.HookConfigFile, error) {
   107		repoRoot, err := resolveInstallRepoRoot(ctx)
   108		if err != nil {
   109			return nil, err
   110		}
   111		return agent.OpenHookConfig(repoRoot, (&ClaudeCodeAgent{}).HookConfigRelPath()) //nolint:wrapcheck // agent.HookConfigFile already names the file in its error
   112	}
   113	
   114	// resolveInstallRepoRoot locates the repo root InstallHooks writes under,
   115	// falling back to CWD when not in a git repo (e.g. during tests).
   116	func resolveInstallRepoRoot(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
   117		// Use repo root instead of CWD to find .claude directory
   118		// This ensures hooks are installed correctly when run from a subdirectory
   119		repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   120		if err == nil {
   121			return repoRoot, nil
   122		}
   123		repoRoot, err = os.Getwd() //nolint:forbidigo // Intentional fallback when WorktreeRoot() fails (tests run outside git repos)
   124		if err != nil {
   125			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current directory: %w", err)
   126		}
   127		return repoRoot, nil
   128	}

   130	// loadRawClaudeSettingsForInstall reads cfg (if present) and returns
   131	// its top-level fields as raw JSON maps, ready for InstallHooks to mutate.
   132	// rawHooks and rawPermissions are always non-nil (empty maps when absent) so
   133	// callers never need a nil check before indexing them.
   134	func loadRawClaudeSettingsForInstall(cfg *agent.HookConfigFile) (rawSettings, rawHooks, rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage, err error) {
   135		existingData, readErr := cfg.Read()
   136		if readErr == nil {
   137			if err := json.Unmarshal(existingData, &rawSettings); err != nil {
   138				return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse existing settings.json: %w", err)
   139			}
   140			// rawHooks preserves unknown hook types (e.g., "Notification")
   141			if hooksRaw, ok := rawSettings["hooks"]; ok {
   142				if err := json.Unmarshal(hooksRaw, &rawHooks); err != nil {
   143					return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hooks in settings.json: %w", err)
   144				}
   145			}

   493	// CheckHookConfig reports whether Entire's Claude Code hooks are absent,
   494	// current, or outdated. It is a read-only diagnostic used by `entire status`
   495	// and `entire doctor`; it never modifies settings. Outdated is detected on the
   496	// positive spec: Entire is installed (Stop hook present) yet one of the current
   497	// tool-use matchers does not carry its Entire hook.

   500		// An unreadable or malformed settings file collapses to HooksAbsent

docs/security-and-privacy.md:18:Which one a repo is on is recorded as `checkpoints.primary.type` in `.entire/settings.json` (or `settings.local.json`); an absent `checkpoints` block means `git-branch`. The redaction described in this document applies identically to both — the pipeline is shared, and only the destination differs. Where the distinction matters below, it is called out.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:84:- Scanner selection is honored **only** from the committed `.entire/settings.json`. A `betterleaks` or `goredact` key present in `.entire/settings.local.json` is ignored, and Entire logs a warning naming the ignored key. This is deliberate: unlike most `settings.local.json` overrides, which are personal and don't affect anyone else, the scanner selection changes what gets redacted into checkpoints that every reader of the repository's history will see — so it has to be a team-visible, committed decision, not a per-developer one.

README.md:494:### settings.local.json (Local Settings)
README.md:555:When a repository has several remotes that could receive checkpoints, interactive first-time `entire enable` asks which one to use, after agent selection and before any hooks or settings are written. Re-running `entire enable` in an enabled repository does not ask again. Choosing a remote saves `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` in `.entire/settings.local.json`, so teammates do not inherit a remote name specific to your clone; keeping the current destination writes nothing.
README.md:588:- Ignore the setting if it looks inherited rather than yours, and fall back to `origin` (or, failing that, the remote you are pushing to). `checkpoint_remote` is normally committed in `.entire/settings.json`, so cloning or forking a project inherits it — without this, a contributor's session data would be pushed into the upstream project's checkpoint repo. A setting is treated as yours when it lives in the gitignored `.entire/settings.local.json`, or when your `origin` **and every push URL** of the remote you are pushing to are owned by the same account or org as the checkpoint repo. Requiring the push destination too covers contributors who cloned the upstream repo and added their own fork, where `origin` belongs to the upstream project rather than to them; requiring every push URL covers mirror-style remotes that fan out to several repositories
README.md:589:- If your checkpoint repo is owned by a different account or org than `origin`, configure it in `.entire/settings.local.json` so it is always honored
README.md:643:- A `settings.local.json` that is **tracked in git** is ignored entirely, and Entire tells you to `git rm --cached` it. `.gitignore` doesn't apply to an already-tracked path, so a committed local file would otherwise override project settings for everyone who clones.

CLAUDE.md:1862:- **OPF's `command` is a trust boundary, not a setting**: `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command` becomes `argv[0]` of an exec during pre-push, and `.entire/settings.json` is version-controlled — so reading it from the project file would let a pull request execute code on every developer who pushes (the prompt is no defense: it never names the command, `prompt_default: "always"` skips it, and non-TTY pushes auto-run). `settings.enforceOPFCommandTrust` (`settings/opf_command_trust.go`) honors `command` only from `.entire/settings.local.json`, and only when that file is untracked in **both** the index and `HEAD` — the filename is not the check, because `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path. The probe goes through go-git (`gitrepo.OpenPath`), not the git CLI, and is memoized per process: shelling out cost ~15 subprocesses per hook (`settings.Load` is uncached and runs several times per hook) and would fail verification wherever `git` is off `$PATH` — the GUI-git-client population that most needs an explicit `command`. **Two depths**: the layer check reads the index only, because a PR-delivered file is always in the index of a clone that checks it out, and checkout cannot produce a file absent from the index; the `command` check also reads HEAD. That split matters because HEAD is the expensive half — measured 8.3ms → 2.5ms per hook process in this repo, and 39ms → 11ms on reftable, where `gitrepo` routes reference reads back through the git CLI. The cost falls on everyone with a `settings.local.json`, not just OPF users, so keep it off the HEAD path. Rejection is a downgrade to the documented `$PATH` default plus a warning, never a hard error; verification failure (no repo, git missing) counts as untrusted. docs/security-and-privacy.md:84:- Scanner selection is honored **only** from the committed `.entire/settings.json`. A `betterleaks` or `goredact` key present in `.entire/settings.local.json` is ignored, and Entire logs a warning naming the ignored key. This is deliberate: unlike most `settings.local.json` overrides, which are personal and don't affect anyone else, the scanner selection changes what gets redacted into checkpoints that every reader of the repository's history will see — so it has to be a team-visible, committed decision, not a per-developer one.

Author:     Suhaan Thayyil <suhaanthayyil0@gmail.com>
AuthorDate: Sun Sep 6 18:27:31 2026 -0400
Commit:     Suhaan Thayyil <suhaanthayyil0@gmail.com>
CommitDate: Sun Sep 6 18:27:31 2026 -0400

    fix: warn when an agent commit lands with no Entire session recorded
    
    PrepareCommitMsg only logged a debug line when it found no session to
    attach a commit to, so the failure (agent session started outside the
    worktree, drifted hook config, an incompatible entire on PATH, etc.)
    was invisible until a user later noticed nothing had been recorded.
    
    Print a visible, rate-limited stderr warning instead, but only when a
    known coding-agent env marker is present (CLAUDECODE, GEMINI_CLI,
    COPILOT_CLI, PI_CODING_AGENT) and no session anywhere in the repo has
    recorded recent activity, so a plain human commit or a healthy
    multi-worktree agent workflow never triggers it.
    
    Fixes #1965

+// HasAgentEnvMarker reports whether the environment carries a marker set by a
+// known coding agent's own process. This answers a different question from
+// isAgentSubprocessEnv above: that one decides "can this process prompt on
+// its inherited TTY" (and so also honors GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, a caller
+// preference rather than an agent identity); this one decides "is a coding
+// agent actually driving this process", used where misidentifying a human's
+// own commit as agent-driven would be the worse mistake (issue #1965: warning
+// when a commit lands with no Entire session recording it).
+//
+//   - CLAUDECODE=1: Claude Code sets this in the environment of every command
+//     it runs.
+//   - GEMINI_CLI=1, COPILOT_CLI=1, PI_CODING_AGENT=true: see
+//     isAgentSubprocessEnv.
+//
+// Markers for other integrations (Cursor, Factory AI Droid, OpenCode, Codex)
+// are not yet verified here and are deliberately omitted rather than guessed:
+// omission means "not detected", not "definitely not an agent".
+func HasAgentEnvMarker() bool {
+	return os.Getenv("CLAUDECODE") != "" ||
+		os.Getenv("GEMINI_CLI") != "" ||
+		os.Getenv("COPILOT_CLI") != "" ||
+		os.Getenv("PI_CODING_AGENT") != ""
+}

+package strategy
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
+

+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

+
+// Issue #1965: when a coding agent commits in an Entire-enabled repo but no
+// session anywhere in the repository has recorded recent activity (e.g. the
+// agent was launched from a bare-clone layout's shared root, outside any
+// worktree, so its hooks never fired), PrepareCommitMsg used to only log a
+// debug line invisible to a normal user before silently skipping the commit.
+// These tests exercise the real hook handler (not a hand-mocked call) end to
+// end and assert a visible stderr warning now appears.
+
+// writeEnabledSettings writes a minimal .entire/settings.json with
+// "enabled": true, matching what `entire enable` produces and what the
+// PersistentPreRun gate in hooks_git_cmd.go requires before any git-hook
+// command reaches the strategy layer in a real invocation.
+func writeEnabledSettings(t *testing.T, dir string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	entireDir := filepath.Join(dir, ".entire")
+	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(entireDir, 0o755))
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(
+		filepath.Join(entireDir, "settings.json"),
+		[]byte(`{"enabled":true}`),
+		0o644,
+	))
+}
+
+// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AgentCommitNoSession_WarnsVisibly is the core
+// regression test for #1965. Setup: a real temp repo (testutil.InitRepo via
+// setupGitRepo), Entire enabled, CLAUDECODE=1 (the real env marker Claude
+// Code sets on every command it runs), and deliberately NO session state
+// anywhere (.git/entire-sessions/ is never populated - no InitializeSession
+// call). PrepareCommitMsg is invoked directly - the actual function a real
+// prepare-commit-msg git hook invocation reaches - with a real commit message
+// file, and stderr is captured through the package's real injectable
+// stderrWriter (the same seam warnStaleEndedSessions already uses).
+//
+// On the fixed code this must produce a visible warning. Run against the
+// pre-fix code (git stash the strategy fix), the captured buffer is empty:
+// the only trace was the debug-level "prepare-commit-msg: no active
+// sessions" log line, invisible to a user reading their terminal.
+func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AgentCommitNoSession_WarnsVisibly(t *testing.T) {
+	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+	writeEnabledSettings(t, dir)
+	t.Setenv("CLAUDECODE", "1")
+
+	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
+
+	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
+	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte("fix: something\n"), 0o644))
+
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	oldWriter := stderrWriter
+	stderrWriter = &buf
+	defer func() { stderrWriter = oldWriter }()
+
+	err := s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	t.Logf("captured stderr: %q", buf.String())
+
+	assert.Contains(t, buf.String(), "no active Entire session",
+		"a coding-agent commit with no session recorded anywhere in the repo must print a visible stderr warning (issue #1965)")
+	assert.Contains(t, buf.String(), "entire doctor",
+		"the warning should point the user at `entire doctor`")
